thread:
marie: customer ticket #23891 — they called our payments API and instead of a refund we created a ledger note (store-only). request_id=req_0abc. attaching payload below.

dan: can you paste the curl + body? which router version?

marie: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments/action -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "user_id": "u-123",
  "amount": 5000,
  "currency": "USD",
  "intent": "refund"
}'

dan: thanks. quick read: the payload omits transaction_id. two server-side tools match this shape: update_account_credit (writes ledger note) and apply_account_credit (creates refund). selector picks the permissive schema match when transaction_id is missing.

kevin: from router logs: selector_v2 scored schema similarity -> update_account_credit (score 0.87) and apply_account_credit (score 0.79). tie-breaker uses alias precedence table which currently ranks update_account_credit higher.

marie: repro steps for SRE/eng to validate:
1) curl payload above (no transaction_id)
2) watch /payments/tool-invoke logs: tool=update_account_credit and response 200 with note_id
3) audit ledger shows a store_note entry, no refund processed

dan: short-term mitigation: push an alias precedence rule to prefer apply_account_credit when intent contains "refund" or "return". longer-term: require transaction_id for update_account_credit schema or use explicit intent signal for router.

linda: billing question — how many customers hit the bad path? we need to reverse ledger notes if money moved.

marie: only one confirmed report so far (ticket #23891). estimated <10 affected calls in last 24h. opened billing job to reverse ledger notes and issue true refunds where needed.

infra-bot: Deploy started: router-alias-rule-2468 -> canary

dan: deployed to canary, monitoring metrics for misroute_count and error_rate

kevin: canary logs (10m window): 0 misroutes, selector now prefers apply_account_credit when intent=refund.

marie: marking thread resolved after billing reversals scheduled. follow-up action: add transaction_id as required field on update_account_credit schema to avoid ambiguous matches and update selector to consider explicit "intent" token more strongly.

kevin: +1 :thumbsup:
